questions.q: Why does Klaff say a pitch has to be simple first?
a: The audience's croc brain takes in the message first
Investors rarely read anything longer than one page
Complex offers are harder to price accurately
Simple pitches make the presenter seem more honest
questions.why: Lesson 1 says a target first picks up your pitch with the croc brain, so what you say must be simple.

questions.q: Which three levels of the brain does the summary describe?
a: Croc brain, midbrain and neocortex
Croc brain, cerebellum and brain stem
Amygdala, hippocampus and neocortex
Midbrain, medulla and prefrontal cortex
questions.why: Lesson 1 traces the brain through the croc brain, the midbrain and finally the neocortex.

questions.q: How do you position yourself as the prize?
a: Show you are not desperate and qualify the buyer
Offer the lowest price before anyone asks
Promise to customize anything the buyer wants
Follow up daily until the deal is signed
questions.why: Lesson 2 says to show you do not depend on the sale and to ask what the customer brings to the deal.

a: Layering several frames to strengthen your point of view
Repeating the same slide until the audience agrees
Letting the buyer set the terms of the meeting
Switching your story whenever you meet resistance
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes throwing multiple frames into a pitch so that your view of the situation wins.

a: Gut decisions people justify only afterward
Facts recalled under pressure during a pitch
Ideas that spread quickly through a company
Arguments that appeal to logical reasoning
questions.why: Lesson 3 says hot cognitions are snap judgments made on intuition and rationalized later.
